admission.authority: direct user continuation of the divisor-layer lift experiment and opportunistic-shortcut policy
admission.reason: Extract the exact N-dependent fixed-gap multiplier hidden inside square divisors of nearby N±d values, with a one-low-bit-mask compression theorem for bounded power-of-two distance windows and exact fallback.

methods.name: BRC local neighbor-square lift fixed-gap shortcut
triggers: large v2 of N plus or minus a small distance
known square divisor of N plus or minus d
capabilities: derive m=2a-epsilon*d from any known a^2 dividing N-epsilon*d
reduce the multiplier-Fermat test to squarehood of mt+1 with fixed gap root abs(a-epsilon*d)
discover the unique signed distance in certain bounded power-of-two neighborhoods using one low-bit mask rather than scanning d
prove that absence of the unique start-level distance prevents every higher power-of-two level from reviving a candidate in the same distance window
enumerate all beyond-horizon power-of-two levels on the unique neighbor when all_levels is requested
probe only multipliers beyond an existing bounded horizon
reuse the exact BALANCED quadratic-residue cascade before isqrt
recover a proper factor by gcd when the exact square witness splits N
return immediately to the ordinary exact fallback on a miss
methods.core_law: If N=a^2 t+epsilon*d with epsilon in {+1,-1} and m=2a-epsilon*d, then mN=a^2(mt+1)-(a-epsilon*d)^2. Therefore mt+1=c^2 gives mN=(ac)^2-(a-epsilon*d)^2. For a0=2^k satisfying 2(a0/2)+D<=H<2a0+D and 2D<a0^2, every beyond-H power-of-two candidate with |d|<=D shares the unique signed residue d determined by N mod a0^2. If that residue lies outside D, no higher power-of-two level can revive a candidate. For H=100,D=64 the exact start level is a0=32, so the full radius-64 distance search reduces to one N mod1024 low-bit observation plus at most one v2 chain.
methods.hard_boundary: This remains a specialization of classical multiplier-Fermat/difference-of-squares inside T0_BRC. The local-window compression removes distance-scan overhead but does not increase the mathematical density of square hits. The committed balanced diagnostic has one horizon-extending hit in the 1009..4999-prime cohort and no hits in the larger 10007..50000 or random-24-bit-prime cohorts at H=100,D=64. It must not replace a complete scan, must not trigger open-ended distance/horizon expansion after a miss, and establishes no asymptotic factorization improvement.
